alerts.title: AKI likely pre-renal, not TDF nephrotoxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines state that in patients on TDF admitted to hospital, intercurrent illnesses with dehydration or sepsis may cause renal function deterioration, in which case TDF may be continued once renal function improves. This patient has severe gastroenteritis with dehydration (BP 90/60, dry mucous membranes), a urea-to-creatinine ratio of 24:1 favouring pre-renal AKI, and urinalysis showing no protein or glucose — atypical for TDF nephrotoxicity, which typically causes proximal tubular dysfunction with proteinuria and glycosuria. Two household contacts share the same illness, supporting infectious gastroenteritis as the cause. Permanently stopping TDF is therefore not indicated by this episode. The guideline recommends checking creatinine (eGFR) in hospitalized TDF patients and continuing TDF if renal function recovers.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue IV fluid resuscitation and treat gastroenteritis. Hold TDF temporarily only if eGFR remains severely impaired; resume TDF once renal function recovers. Do not permanently discontinue TDF for this pre-renal AKI episode.

alerts.title: If TDF must be stopped, use guideline-recommended substitute
alerts.message: Guidelines specify that if renal impairment develops due to TDF, the recommended alternative regimen is ABC + 3TC + DTG. If the clinician decides to discontinue TDF based on this AKI episode, the regimen should be switched to ABC + 3TC + DTG rather than simply stopping TDF without replacement, which would leave an incomplete regimen and risk virological failure in a patient currently suppressed (<50 copies/mL).

evidence.recommended_action: If TDF is discontinued, switch to ABC + 3TC + DTG as the guideline-recommended alternative. Confirm ABC hypersensitivity risk (HLA-B*5701 if available) before initiating abacavir.

alerts.title: DTG creatinine rise does not apply here
alerts.message: Guidelines describe a benign DTG-related creatinine rise of <30 µmol/L occurring within the first month of initiation, which does not progress after that. This patient has been on DTG for 2 years with previously normal creatinine (0.9 mg/dL), and the current rise to 2.4 mg/dL represents an increase of ~133 µmol/L — far exceeding the DTG-related threshold and occurring acutely with dehydration. This pattern is inconsistent with DTG-related creatinine elevation and supports an alternative cause.

evidence.recommended_action: Do not attribute this AKI to DTG. The magnitude and timing are inconsistent with DTG-related creatinine rise. Focus on resuscitation and treating the infectious cause.
